title: AF-2-part-3
description: Airframe exam covering composite materials and repair (fibers, resins, layup, curing, honeycomb structures), non-destructive testing methods, corrosion theory and treatment, and transparent plastics, drawn from the AF-2 composites/corrosion/NDT question/answer bank.

questions.question: A unidirectional (tape) reinforcing composite material has its highest strength in what direction?
options: A. Perpendicular to the fiber direction
questions.explanation: Unidirectional tape has all its reinforcing fibers aligned one way, so strength is highest along that fiber direction and much lower across it.

questions.question: Which reinforcing fabric is available only as a prepreg tape product (not as a dry woven fabric)?
questions.explanation: Boron fiber is typically supplied only as a prepreg tape due to its stiffness and the difficulty of weaving it into fabric.

questions.question: Which of the following composite reinforcement fibers has high impact resistance?
questions.explanation: Aramid fibers are valued for their high impact and abrasion resistance, often used where toughness is more important than pure stiffness.

questions.question: Which practice does NOT help minimize residual stress in metal during cure of the resin?
options: A. Designing a symmetrical, balanced laminate
B. Controlling the cure temperature profile
questions.explanation: A non-symmetrical laminate layup tends to warp and induce residual stress during cure; symmetrical, balanced layups help minimize this.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of cleaning a composite/metal surface?
options: B. That cleaning helps prevent corrosion
C. That cleaning can be used in place of a paint finish
questions.explanation: Cleaning prepares a surface for bonding or painting; it does not substitute for a protective paint finish.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required for electrochemical (galvanic) corrosion to form?
options: C. A specific metal surface finish type
questions.explanation: Galvanic corrosion requires dissimilar metals, an electrolyte, and electrical contact; the specific surface finish of the metal is not a fundamental requirement.

questions.question: What is a thin layer of fiberglass used with a repair part to create a clean surface for the bonding process?
questions.explanation: Peel ply is bonded to the laminate surface and peeled away just before final bonding, leaving a clean, textured surface ready for adhesion.

questions.question: What is a cause of delamination in a composite/honeycomb structure?
options: A. Water trapped in the honeycomb core
B. Excessive cleaning of the surface
C. Using too little resin color pigment
questions.explanation: Water that enters and freezes/expands within the honeycomb core is a common cause of delamination between the skin and core.

questions.question: The recommended time at room temperature to complete layup and compaction of a prepreg is called what?
questions.explanation: Handling life (out-time) is the limited period a prepreg can be worked with at room temperature before it must be cured or returned to cold storage.

questions.question: What type of drill bit is recommended for drilling acrylic plastic?
options: A. A standard twist drill with a 118° included angle
B. A twist drill ground with a 150° included angle
C. A spade bit with a 90° point
questions.explanation: Acrylic requires a specially ground drill bit with a wider (about 150°) included angle and polished flutes to prevent cracking and overheating.

questions.question: What test is used to determine if a surface has been thoroughly cleaned before bonding?
questions.explanation: In the water break test, water sheeting evenly across a surface (rather than beading) indicates the surface is clean and free of contaminants.

questions.question: Which fastener type is commonly used for sealing joints in a fuel tank?
options: C. Interference-fit wet-installed fasteners (e.g., "E-Z Buck" style)
questions.explanation: Special wet-installed, interference-fit fasteners are used in fuel tank areas to maintain a fuel-tight seal at the joint.

questions.question: Which fiber type is used for composite materials that must operate at very high temperatures?
questions.explanation: Ceramic fibers retain strength at very high temperatures where organic fibers like aramid or standard glass would degrade.

questions.question: What is the most commonly used type of resin in aircraft composite structures?
questions.explanation: Epoxy resin is the most widely used matrix resin in aerospace composites due to its strength, durability, and good bonding properties.

questions.question: What tool is used to impregnate resin into dry fabric during a wet layup?
questions.explanation: A squeegee is used to work and spread resin evenly into the dry fabric plies during a wet layup process.

questions.question: Acetone, toluol, and MEK (methyl ethyl ketone) are characterized by what property?
questions.explanation: These common composite-shop solvents are highly volatile and flammable, meaning they have a low flash point and require careful handling.

questions.question: Which of the following is a material NOT used for curing composite repairs?
options: B. A vacuum fixture (used for shaping/clamping, not curing itself)
questions.explanation: A vacuum fixture is used to apply shape and pressure during bonding, not as a curing heat source like an oven or heat blanket.

questions.question: What is the first stage of corrosion removal from a metal surface?
questions.explanation: Before corrosion can be assessed or treated, the surface must first be cleaned and any paint stripped to expose the base metal.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about wet layup?
options: A. A dry fabric is impregnated with resin at the time of layup
B. The fabric is pre-impregnated at the factory
C. No resin is used in wet layup
questions.explanation: In a wet layup, dry reinforcing fabric is saturated with resin on-site as it is laid up, as opposed to using factory pre-impregnated (prepreg) material.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about a potted repair?
options: A. It is used only for damage larger than 12 inches
B. It requires complete removal of the honeycomb core across the whole panel
C. It is used to repair damage up to about 1 inch in size
questions.explanation: A potted compound repair is a simple, limited repair method typically reserved for small damage areas, roughly up to 1 inch.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about composite structures?
options: A. That they can be tailored for directional strength
B. That they provide a lower strength-to-weight ratio than metal
C. That they generally resist fatigue well
questions.explanation: Composite structures typically offer a higher (not lower) strength-to-weight ratio compared with equivalent metal structures.

questions.question: Which compartment commonly requires neutralizing of acidic residuals?
questions.explanation: Lead-acid battery compartments accumulate acidic residue/fumes that must be neutralized (e.g., with baking soda) during cleaning and corrosion treatment.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a corrosion treatment practice?
options: A. Treating a Ni-Cad (nickel-cadmium) battery compartment with an acid-neutralizing agent meant for lead-acid batteries
B. Neutralizing acid spills in lead-acid battery compartments with baking soda
C. Applying protective coatings after cleaning corrosion
questions.explanation: Ni-Cad battery compartments require an alkaline electrolyte neutralizer (such as boric acid solution), not the acid-neutralizing treatment used for lead-acid batteries.

questions.question: When comparing carbon fiber to fiberglass, carbon fiber generally has what kind of stiffness and strength?
questions.explanation: Carbon fiber generally offers greater stiffness and strength compared with fiberglass, though it is more brittle and can be more expensive.

questions.question: What indicates the longitudinal fibers of a fabric and the high-strength direction?
questions.explanation: Warp fibers run the length of the fabric roll and represent the primary high-strength direction, referenced using a "warp clock."

questions.question: Why can't carbon fiber face sheets be used directly in contact with an aluminum honeycomb core?
options: A. Because carbon fiber is not strong enough
B. Because carbon fiber cannot be bonded with adhesive
C. Because it causes the aluminum to corrode (galvanic corrosion)
questions.explanation: Carbon fiber is cathodic relative to aluminum, so direct contact sets up galvanic corrosion that attacks the aluminum core; an isolation layer is required.

questions.question: Which materials are commonly used to repair bonded metal honeycomb structure skins?
questions.explanation: Metal honeycomb repairs commonly use metallic face sheet materials such as aluminum, steel, or titanium to match the original structure.

questions.question: Which inspection method needs closer examination using tools such as flashlights and magnifying glasses?
questions.explanation: Visual inspection relies on direct observation, aided by tools like flashlights and magnifiers, to detect surface defects.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about repairing small damage in plastics (such as acrylic)?
options: A. Cracks in plastic never need any repair action
B. A small crack's growth can be stopped by stop-drilling a small hole at the extreme ends of the crack
C. Cracks must always be repaired by replacing the entire panel
questions.explanation: Stop-drilling a small hole at the tip of a crack relieves stress concentration and halts further crack propagation in plastics like acrylic.

questions.question: Penetrant inspection is generally NOT suitable for use on what kind of materials?
questions.explanation: Porous materials absorb the penetrant into the material itself rather than just surface defects, making penetrant inspection unreliable on them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about carbon fiber?
options: A. That it is electrically non-conductive
B. That it has high stiffness and strength
C. That it can cause galvanic corrosion when in contact with aluminum
questions.explanation: Carbon fiber is actually electrically conductive, which is part of why it can promote galvanic corrosion when placed in contact with aluminum.

questions.question: Why are composite materials generally not used on the leading edges of an aircraft wing?
options: A. Because composites are too heavy for that location
B. Because composite materials/structures have lower erosion resistance
C. Because composites cannot be shaped to an airfoil leading edge
questions.explanation: Leading edges are exposed to rain, hail, and debris erosion; composites typically have lower erosion resistance than metal in that highly exposed location.

questions.question: In galvanic corrosion, which metal tends to corrode (is sacrificed)?
questions.explanation: In a galvanic cell, the more active (less noble) metal acts as the anode and corrodes, protecting the more noble cathode metal.

questions.question: How should plastic materials typically be cleaned?
options: B. With plenty of water and mild soap
questions.explanation: Plastics like acrylic are cleaned with copious water and mild soap to avoid solvent-induced crazing or abrasive scratching.

questions.question: Because acrylic plastic conducts heat poorly, what precaution should be taken when drilling it?
options: A. Drill at the highest possible speed with no cooling
B. Make provisions for removing the heat generated while drilling
C. Avoid using any drill bit specifically made for acrylic
questions.explanation: Poor heat conduction in acrylic means heat builds up locally during drilling, so cooling/heat removal provisions help prevent cracking or crazing.

questions.question: What tool is used to cut plastic material into curved shapes?
questions.explanation: A band saw's continuous blade allows controlled curved cuts in plastic sheet material.

questions.question: Which environment tends to increase the rate of corrosion the most?
questions.explanation: Marine environments combine moisture and salt (a strong electrolyte), significantly accelerating corrosion compared with dry climates.

questions.question: A defect such as a bend/crease line caused by the insertion of adhesive paper during handling is classified as what?
questions.explanation: Damage introduced during handling/service (like a crease from inserted material) is classified as an in-service defect rather than one from original manufacturing.

questions.question: What is the maximum time a prepreg can be kept at room temperature before use, often called what term?
questions.explanation: Mechanical/handling life (out-time) is the cumulative time a prepreg can spend at room temperature before its resin properties degrade.

questions.question: What type of repair restores the required strength of a structure but not necessarily its full durability/service life?
questions.explanation: A temporary repair restores adequate strength for continued safe operation but is expected to be replaced later with a permanent repair.

questions.question: What is true about using ultrasonic testing to detect a defect in a composite laminate?
options: A. It always requires two technicians on opposite sides of the part
B. The pulse-echo method using a single transducer is a common technique
C. It cannot detect internal delamination
questions.explanation: Pulse-echo ultrasonic testing, using a single transducer that both sends and receives the sound pulse, is a standard method for detecting internal defects like delamination.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a heat-curing tool used in composite repair?
options: A. A vacuum bag (applies pressure, not heat)
questions.explanation: A vacuum bag applies compaction pressure during cure; it is not itself a heat source, unlike heat blankets or curing ovens.

questions.question: What is vacuum fixture molding?
options: A. A process using only mechanical clamps for pressure
B. A process in which the layup is cured under pressure generated by drawing a vacuum on the repair
C. A process that eliminates the need for any resin
questions.explanation: Vacuum fixture molding uses the pressure differential from a drawn vacuum to compact and cure the composite layup against a form or fixture.

questions.question: Which type of honeycomb core cell shape is used for parts with simple curves?
questions.explanation: Standard rectangular/hexagonal honeycomb core is suitable for parts with simple, gentle curves, while more flexible core shapes handle complex curvature.

questions.question: Which type of adhesive can typically be kept at room temperature without refrigeration?
questions.explanation: Unlike many film adhesives that require cold storage, two-part paste adhesives are often formulated to be stored and mixed at room temperature.

questions.question: How do you remove hydraulic fluid, grease, or fuel contamination from aircraft tires?
options: A. Using straight gasoline as a cleaner
B. Washing with a mild soap solution
C. Using a wire brush and strong solvent
questions.explanation: Tire rubber is sensitive to petroleum solvents, so contamination is removed with a mild soap and water solution rather than harsh solvents.

questions.question: What is the major safety risk associated with radiographic (X-ray) inspection?
questions.explanation: Radiographic inspection uses ionizing radiation, so radiation exposure to personnel is the primary safety concern requiring shielding and controlled access.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about tap testing a honeycomb sandwich composite part?
options: A. That a well-bonded, solid structure produces a thud-like (dull) sound
B. That a disbonded area produces a different, hollow/dead sound
C. That tap testing is a simple, low-cost inspection method
questions.explanation: A well-bonded, solid structure actually produces a clear, sharp ("ringing") sound, while a disbonded or delaminated area produces the dull, thud-like sound — the opposite of this statement.

questions.question: Acrylic, the transparent material commonly used for windows and canopies, is also known by what trade name?
questions.explanation: Acrylic sheet used for aircraft windows and canopies is commonly known by the trade name Plexiglass.

questions.question: Which curing cycle is typically used for prepreg composite materials?
questions.explanation: Most aerospace prepreg resin systems require elevated temperature (and often pressure) to fully cure and develop their design properties.

questions.question: What material is used to absorb vibration during installation of replacement plastic panels?
options: C. Loose fitting with no cushioning material
questions.explanation: A cushioning material like cork or gasket strip is placed between a rigid plastic panel and its frame to absorb vibration and prevent stress cracking.

questions.question: What is the storage requirement for transparent plastics such as acrylic sheet?
options: A. Store near heat sources for flexibility
B. No special storage precautions are needed
C. Store in a cool location (away from heat and direct sun)
questions.explanation: Transparent plastics should be stored in a cool location, shielded from heat and UV exposure, to prevent warping, yellowing, or crazing.

questions.question: A composite made of thin face sheets bonded to a thicker honeycomb core is called what type of structure?
questions.explanation: This construction, thin skins bonded to a lightweight core, is called sandwich construction, widely used for its high stiffness-to-weight ratio.

questions.question: What is true about bonded metal honeycomb composite repair?
options: A. It is normally an in-situ repair technique that closely restores original structural characteristics using high-temperature cured adhesive, vacuum bag, and pre-cured laminate or metal sheet
B. It can never be performed on the aircraft (always requires removal)
C. It never uses adhesive, only mechanical fasteners
questions.explanation: Bonded metal honeycomb repairs are typically done in place on the aircraft, using heat, vacuum bagging, and adhesive to closely restore original structural performance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of metal bonded honeycomb composite construction?
options: B. High stiffness for the weight
questions.explanation: Metal bonded honeycomb actually provides a superior (greater, not lesser) strength-to-weight ratio, which is one of its key advantages.

questions.question: What is the purpose of vacuum bagging in a composite repair?
options: A. To add extra resin to the laminate
B. To remove trapped air between plies and hold the plies together under pressure during cure
C. To heat the laminate directly
questions.explanation: Vacuum bagging draws out trapped air and volatiles while applying consistent compaction pressure, improving laminate quality during cure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about ultrasonic testing?
options: A. That it can detect internal delamination and voids
B. That it uses high-frequency sound waves above the audible range
C. That ultrasonic sound waves can be transmitted through a vacuum
questions.explanation: Sound waves, including ultrasonic waves, require a physical medium to travel and cannot be transmitted through a vacuum, unlike electromagnetic radiation.

questions.question: Anomalies such as porosity, micro-cracking, and delamination resulting from processing discrepancies are classified as what?
questions.explanation: Defects traced back to problems during the original fabrication/curing process are classified as manufacturing defects, distinct from in-service damage.

questions.question: What material is used so that prepreg or wet layup plies do not stick to the working surface or caul plate?
questions.explanation: A solid release film prevents the uncured laminate from bonding to the tool surface or caul plate while still allowing it to be removed cleanly after cure.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is arranged in increasing order of cathodic (noble) property?
questions.explanation: On the galvanic series, aluminum is quite anodic (active), copper is more noble, and gold is among the most cathodic (noble) metals, in that increasing order.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT used for corrosion treatment?
options: B. A lead-acid battery (itself a source of corrosive acid, not a treatment)
questions.explanation: A lead-acid battery is a source of corrosive electrolyte that must be neutralized after a spill; it is not itself a corrosion treatment material.

questions.question: A form of corrosion resulting in general roughening or pitting of a metal surface, often with a powdery deposit of corrosion products, is called what?
questions.explanation: Surface corrosion is the common, general attack that roughens or pits a metal surface and leaves a powdery corrosion product (such as aluminum oxide).

questions.question: Which environmental condition does NOT increase the rate of corrosion?
options: C. An environment with trapped moisture
questions.explanation: Dry conditions, lacking the moisture/electrolyte needed for electrochemical reactions, generally do not promote corrosion, unlike humid or salty environments.

questions.question: Which inspection method involves magnetic fields and circulating (induced) currents?
questions.explanation: Eddy current inspection induces circulating electrical currents in a conductive part using a magnetic field, and changes in those currents reveal flaws.

questions.question: What tool is typically used to cut prepreg and dry composite fabrics?
questions.explanation: Prepreg and dry fabric plies are commonly trimmed to shape with scissors (or specialized fabric shears/cutters).

questions.question: Which composite reinforcement material has a distinctive white color appearance?
questions.explanation: Fiberglass reinforcement has a characteristic white or off-white appearance, unlike black carbon fiber or yellow aramid fiber.

questions.question: Which honeycomb core cell size provides better support to the sandwich face sheets?
options: C. Cell size has no effect on face sheet support
questions.explanation: Smaller honeycomb cells provide more frequent, closely spaced support points to the thin face sheets, improving their resistance to dimpling or buckling.

questions.question: Which core material is NOT commonly used on commercial transport category aircraft?
questions.explanation: While foam cores are used in some general aviation and non-structural applications, aluminum and Nomex honeycomb are far more common in commercial transport structures.

questions.question: A composite containing two or more different types of reinforcing fiber bound in the same matrix is commonly known as what?
questions.explanation: Hybrid composites combine different fiber types (e.g., carbon and aramid) in one matrix to balance properties such as stiffness and impact resistance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an in-service defect?
options: A. A manufacturing void from the autoclave cycle
C. A resin-rich area from initial layup
questions.explanation: Delamination occurring after the part is in use, from impact or moisture ingress for example, is classified as an in-service defect.

questions.question: Envelope bagging is a process in which what happens?
options: A. Only the repair patch is bagged, leaving the rest of the part exposed
B. The part being repaired is completely enclosed within the vacuum bag
C. No vacuum is used at all
questions.explanation: In envelope bagging, the entire part (not just the local repair area) is enclosed inside the vacuum bag for curing.

questions.question: Which honeycomb core cell configuration is stiffer and stronger?
questions.explanation: Standard beveled hexagonal cells provide greater inherent stiffness and strength compared with the more flexible over-expanded core designed for curved parts.

questions.question: What color is characteristic of aramid fiber?
questions.explanation: Aramid fiber (e.g., Kevlar) has a distinctive yellow/gold color, distinguishing it visually from white fiberglass and black carbon fiber.

questions.question: Resin starvation in a laminate could be a result of what?
options: A. Excessive resin application during layup
B. Using too much bleeder ply
C. Insufficient resin application during layup
questions.explanation: If not enough resin is applied or too much is removed during cure, the laminate can become resin-starved, leaving dry fibers and reduced strength.

questions.question: What vacuum bagging material is used to collect excess resin and create a path for air to escape from the repair?
questions.explanation: Bleeder ply absorbs excess resin drawn out during cure and provides a path for trapped air/volatiles to escape under vacuum.

questions.question: What is a good example of electrochemical (galvanic) attack?
options: A. Uniform surface oxidation of a single metal
C. A simple galvanic cell (two dissimilar metals with an electrolyte)
questions.explanation: A simple galvanic cell, with two dissimilar metals in electrical contact through an electrolyte, is the classic example of electrochemical (galvanic) corrosion.

questions.question: Which inspection method uses sound wave energy to detect flaws?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic inspection uses high-frequency sound waves transmitted through the material to detect internal flaws such as voids and delamination.

questions.question: What is used to apply the necessary pressure to pre-bonded honeycomb repairs?
options: C. A vacuum fixture (or vacuum bag)
questions.explanation: A vacuum fixture (vacuum bag assembly) applies the consistent pressure needed to properly bond pre-bonded honeycomb repair patches.

questions.question: What is used to shorten the curing time of bonded honeycomb repairs from roughly 12 hours down to about 1 hour?
questions.explanation: Infrared heat lamps accelerate the cure by providing controlled, elevated heat directly to the repair area, dramatically reducing cure time.

questions.question: What hazard is associated with using infrared heat lamps to cure bonded honeycomb repairs?
options: A. A high temperature differential between the repair and surrounding area may cause buckling of the surrounding skin from thermal expansion
B. The repair area becomes too cold to cure
C. Infrared lamps cannot cure adhesive at all
questions.explanation: Localized intense heating from an IR lamp can create a steep temperature gradient, inducing thermal expansion stresses that buckle the surrounding skin.

questions.question: Why is damage inspection more critical for honeycomb assemblies than for conventional (solid skin) structures?
options: A. Honeycomb is always visually obvious when damaged
B. Honeycomb structures cannot be damaged at all
C. Honeycomb assemblies may suffer extensive internal damage without any observable external indication
questions.explanation: Because honeycomb core can crush or disbond internally while the outer skin shows little or no visible sign, careful inspection is critical to catch hidden damage.

questions.question: Which honeycomb core cell shape is used to form panels with complex compound curves?
questions.explanation: Flexible, bell-shaped (over-expanded) core cells can conform to complex, compound-curved panel shapes better than standard hexagonal cells.

questions.question: What is an isotropic material?
options: A. A material that is strong only along one fiber direction
B. A material whose properties vary by location but not direction
C. A material that has uniform properties in all directions
questions.explanation: Isotropic materials, like most metals, exhibit the same mechanical properties regardless of the direction in which they are tested.

questions.question: A laminate made up of layers of two or more different homogeneous reinforcement materials is called what?
questions.explanation: An inter-ply hybrid combines different reinforcement types layer by layer (ply by ply) within the same laminate stack.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about non-woven abrasive materials?
options: A. That they are useful for light surface cleaning and blending
B. That different grades offer different levels of abrasiveness
C. That a lacquer-impregnated webbing pad can be used to clean corroded aluminum surfaces (actually a non-impregnated or appropriate abrasive pad should be used, not a lacquer-based one)
questions.explanation: Using a lacquer-impregnated pad on corroded aluminum is not correct practice; appropriate non-woven abrasive pads (without lacquer contamination) are used for this cleaning task.

questions.question: When tows of two or more constituent fiber types are mixed within the same fabric layer, this is called what?
questions.explanation: Intra-ply hybrids blend different fiber types together within a single ply/layer, as opposed to stacking separate plies of different materials (inter-ply).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about composite materials?
options: A. That they cannot be damaged by sonic/vibration energy
B. That they can be damaged by impact
C. That they can suffer from delamination
questions.explanation: Composite materials can in fact be damaged by sonic/vibration energy over time (e.g., disbonding from engine or acoustic vibration); this statement is false.

questions.question: What is the use of a router in honeycomb repair?
questions.explanation: A router is used to precisely trim away damaged skin and core material, creating a clean, properly shaped cavity for the repair.

questions.question: In which direction is a composite material generally strong and stiff?
options: A. Equally in every direction regardless of fiber orientation
B. In the same direction as the fiber orientation
C. Only perpendicular to the fiber direction
questions.explanation: A composite's strength and stiffness are governed by fiber orientation; it is strongest along the direction the fibers run.

questions.question: What inspection method uses sound wave energy with a frequency above the audible range?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic inspection uses sound frequencies above human hearing (ultrasound) to probe materials for internal defects.

questions.question: Which of the following is an isotropic material?
questions.explanation: Metals such as aluminum are isotropic, having the same properties in all directions, unlike directional fiber-reinforced composites.

questions.question: In honeycomb construction, increasing the core thickness primarily and greatly increases what property?
questions.explanation: A thicker honeycomb core increases the overall panel's effective depth, which greatly increases bending stiffness for a given face sheet weight.

questions.question: What is used to neutralize acid deposits in a lead-acid battery compartment?
questions.explanation: Baking soda solution is an alkaline neutralizer used to counteract and clean up acidic electrolyte deposits in lead-acid battery compartments.

questions.question: Which type of tool is NOT recommended for working on carbon fiber composite material?
options: A. An electrical motor-driven tool lacking proper dust/spark control (conductive dust hazard)
C. A pneumatic tool with dust extraction
questions.explanation: Carbon fiber dust is electrically conductive and can pose hazards to unshielded electrical equipment, so uncontrolled electrical power tools are avoided in favor of properly equipped or non-electrical tools.

questions.question: Which materials are used as coatings for sacrificial (galvanic) protection of underlying metal?
questions.explanation: Cadmium and zinc are more anodic than many structural metals, so they are applied as sacrificial coatings that corrode preferentially, protecting the base metal.

questions.question: What is the most common fastener alloy used with carbon fiber reinforced composite structures?
questions.explanation: Titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V is galvanically compatible with carbon fiber and offers high strength, making it the preferred fastener material for CFRP structures.

questions.question: What is a typical curing temperature for many aerospace composite materials?
questions.explanation: A commonly cited curing temperature for many epoxy prepreg composite systems is around 250°F (roughly 121°C), among other cure schedules used.

questions.question: Which fasteners are similar in design to Hi-Loks and are a natural choice for carbon fiber composite structures?
questions.explanation: Eddie-Bolt fasteners share the pin-and-collar design philosophy of Hi-Loks, making them well suited for the high-strength, low-clearance needs of composite joints.

questions.question: The strength and stiffness of a composite buildup mainly depends on what?
options: A. The color of the resin used
B. The brand of fabric used
C. The orientation sequence of the plies
questions.explanation: Laminate strength and stiffness are engineered through the stacking sequence and fiber orientation of each ply in the layup.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about composite materials?
options: A. That each component (fiber and matrix) is merged completely and cannot be identified physically
B. That the fiber and matrix remain distinguishable constituents
C. That properties depend on both the fiber and the resin matrix
questions.explanation: In a composite, the fiber and matrix remain physically distinct constituents bonded together; they do not merge into a single indistinguishable material.

questions.question: What is the high-strength fiber direction due to the straightness of the fibers in a woven fabric called?
questions.explanation: Warp fibers run straight along the length of the fabric roll, giving that direction the highest strength due to minimal fiber crimp.

questions.question: What tools are used to impregnate dry fibers with resin during a wet layup?
options: C. A brush and a squeegee
questions.explanation: A brush is often used to initially wet out the fabric, with a squeegee used afterward to work the resin thoroughly through the plies and remove excess.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an elevated-temperature curing prepreg process?
options: A. A refrigerator (used for storage, not curing itself)
B. A curing oven or autoclave
questions.explanation: A refrigerator is used to store uncured prepreg material before use, not as part of the actual elevated-temperature curing process.

questions.question: Which type of plastic does not soften appreciably under heat but may char and blister at about 400-500°F (240-260°C)?
questions.explanation: Thermosetting plastics undergo an irreversible cure and, once set, resist softening under heat, though they will char/blister at high enough temperatures.

questions.question: Which type of plastic softens under heat and can be dissolved in various organic solvents?
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics can be repeatedly softened by heat and are generally soluble in appropriate organic solvents, unlike cured thermosetting plastics.
